title: A Sigil for the Veil Again
premise: Astrid Ishikawa has survived a decade in the magic-hating city of Vell by being unremarkable: a royal food-taster with a carefully built tolerance to poison, and a discreet seller of harmless little charms. When the outlawed old gods suddenly begin answering prayers again, Astrid's small magics flare into something undeniable, and the Crown's witch-hunters turn their attention to the taster's kitchen. Hunted alongside the found family of charm-buyers who shelter them, Astrid learns the gods are returning because the country itself is dying—Vell was built over a door the founders sealed, and the long winter falling is the seal failing. To save the people they love, Astrid must find and open the door out of a country that no longer exists, choosing truth and identity over the invisibility that kept them safe, and ending the story by leading their family through the threshold into a land where magic—and Astrid—need not hide.
about_author: Mara Yarrow is the pen name of a former line cook who swears the kitchen taught her more about magic than any grimoire. She writes quiet, hungry fantasy about people who survive by being underestimated.

chapters.title: The Taster's Tongue
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. We meet them in the royal kitchens, tasting the queen's breakfast, cataloguing poisons, and slipping a luck-charm to a scullery boy on the sly. The emotional beat is the comfort of routine and the quiet loneliness of a life built on being no one.

chapters.title: Prayers, Answered
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. A dying beggar's desperate prayer to a forgotten god is answered through one of Astrid's trinkets, which blazes with real power. Terrified and exhilarated, Astrid realizes their charms were never fake. The beat is wonder curdling into fear as the city's bells announce a witch-finding.

chapters.title: The Charm-Row Family
chapters.summary: Alternating POV with Odessa, a fence who sells Astrid's charms and mothers the neighborhood's strays. The witch-hunters raid Charm Row; Odessa burns her ledger to protect her buyers. The beat is found family choosing each other as the noose tightens.

chapters.title: What the Queen Dreams
chapters.summary: The queen's POV. Haunted by dreams of a door beneath the palace, she summons her food-taster, and Astrid recognizes in her the same returning-god dreams. The beat is uneasy kinship between two women pretending to be smaller than they are.

chapters.title: Snow in the First Month
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Winter arrives impossibly early and does not stop; crops fail, and the hunt intensifies as the Crown blames magic. Astrid's immunity to poison is exposed as sorcery when they survive an assassination meant for the queen. The beat is identity stripped bare—Astrid is seen, and seen is doomed.

chapters.title: The Cartographer of Doors
chapters.summary: Odessa's POV. The family shelters a mad old priest who once mapped the sealed door beneath Vell. He confirms the winter is the seal failing and the country is already, in the gods' eyes, no more. The beat is loyalty tested: flee and live, or stay and seek a door that may not exist.

chapters.title: Beneath the Palace Stones
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Guided by the queen's dreams and the priest's map, Astrid and Odessa descend into the flooded foundations, pursued by the witch-finder Halvard. The gods speak to Astrid directly, offering the truth of their own forgotten name. The beat is the seduction and terror of being fully known.

chapters.title: The Price of the Threshold
chapters.summary: Halvard's POV. The witch-finder catches them at the door and reveals he was once a charm-seller too, broken by the same gods' silence. He demands Astrid renounce magic publicly in exchange for the family's lives. The beat is the book's moral crux: loyalty versus truth, safety versus self.

chapters.title: A Sigil for the Veil
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV, climax. Refusing to lie, Astrid carves their true name into the door and offers their built immunity—every poison they ever swallowed—as the key. The seal breaks; the winter pauses mid-fall; Halvard, weeping, chooses to hold the witch-hunters back. The beat is sacrifice transmuted into self-acceptance.

chapters.title: The Country That Is Not on Any Map
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. Astrid, Odessa, the queen, and Charm Row's strays step through the door into a spring country where the old gods wait with open hands. Astrid keeps their name, their family, and their magic. The beat is quiet resolution: home was never the city—it was the people who saw you and stayed.
